items.title: A day in the life of a Cryogenic Systems Engineer
items.summary:
In August 2026, IBM successfully connected and cooled two cryogenic modules into a single operating environment: 
https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/modular-cryogenics
 
The achievement validates a fundamental design principle behind the IBM Quantum roadmap: Quantum computers of the future should be built as modular systems.
 
Instead of housing processors inside isolated cryostats, our architecture creates connected cryogenic cells that can be linked together while maintaining the ultra-cold temperatures required for quantum computation.
 
In this video, IBM Quantum Cryogenic Assembly Engineer Allie Lindler answers some of our most frequently asked questions about this new modular approach to housing and cooling quantum processors, including what it takes to achieve and maintain scalable, ultracold temperatures as a cryogenics specialist.

items.title: HISTORIC: DRDO Builds a Chip Smaller Than a Fingernail That Can Power India's Next Radar System
items.summary:
DRDO has developed indigenous Gallium Nitride technology, a major leap forward for India's radar and defense systems.

The Defence Research and Development Organisation has demonstrated a new 3.5x3 mm chip capable of delivering up to 30W of power. This advancement supports high-frequency operations up to X-band, providing superior power density compared to traditional silicon. By utilizing indigenous 4-inch silicon carbide wafers, the Gallium Arsenide Enabling Technology Centre in Hyderabad is now establishing limited production for these critical components.

Developing indigenous Gallium Nitride technology is a strategic move to secure India's supply chain and bypass foreign export controls. While this demonstration marks a significant milestone for defense electronics, the focus now shifts to scaling production for reliable, mass-market deployment. This capability is essential for modern electronic warfare systems, ensuring that India's semiconductor manufacturing infrastructure remains resilient and self-reliant.

items.title: The Reason Most Always-On AI Agents Die in Two Weeks (with Dilani Kahawala)
items.summary:
#aiagents #aiassistant #aistartup 

In Episode #1027, Dr. Dilani Kahawala (Co-Founder and CEO of Anna) joins @JonKrohnLearns explain what it takes to build an always-on AI assistant that busy parents will trust with their inboxes. Anna watches the email, school apps, WhatsApp messages and calendars flowing into a family's life and surfaces what matters, over text and voice, with barely any app to speak of. Dilani came to it by way of a Harvard physics PhD, McKinsey, and a decade of product leadership at Etsy, Meta and Atlassian, and says she has had to throw away most of what that decade taught her about how products get built. In this episode, she lays out the three hardest problems in building Anna, why the eval loop is the heart of the product, how a long-running agent differs from a turn-based one, and the brutal unit economics of consumer AI.

items.title: Inside quantum optimization research
items.summary:
Optimization is often cited as one of quantum computing’s most promising applications. Businesses and researchers are constantly searching for better routes, schedules, allocations, and ways to allocate limited resources, meaning that a computational advantage for quantum optimization methods could deliver enormous value. Yet despite years of research, fundamental questions remain: Which optimization problems are best suited to quantum computers? And how will we know when quantum methods have truly surpassed their classical counterparts? 

 

In this episode of the Coherence Times, we’re joined by IBM’s Stefan Wörner and Stephanie Riedmüller of the Zuse Institute to explore the promise and limitations of quantum optimization. Together, they discuss the search for new quantum algorithms, the importance of benchmarking and community-driven research, and what it will take for quantum computers to deliver practical advantages for real-world optimization problems.  

Learn more about quantum computing and explore the IBM Quantum Platform → https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com 

Are you an optimization researcher? Contribute to the Quantum Optimization Benchmarking Library → https://github.com/ZIB-AOPT/QOBLIB

items.title: Why Voice AI Still Needs a Screen | Pavan Muddireddy
items.summary:
Ordering food by voice alone is harder than it sounds: without a menu in front of you, you have to hold every item in your head while you decide. Pavankumar Reddy Muddireddy, who leads audio research at Mistral AI, uses that example to explain why he expects voice to sit on top of a screen rather than replace it. The screen lets you take in information quickly and gives you proof that the system did what it said.

Watch the full conversation with Pavan:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ixu0H8bsCts

The full episode was produced in partnership with Mistral AI.
